title: A full walk check that gets stopped picks up where it stopped instead of starting over
goal: When the once-a-day full walk check is stopped because the person came back to the Mac, the next run only does the walks it never reached (and the few that failed at the end), so five hours of checking are not thrown away for twenty missing walks and the loop gets back to building sooner.
notes: The user asked 'how did we get paused like this' on 2026-10-22 at 09:20. Cause: after the scene task ended at 04:14 the loop started the daily full walk check (queue/bin/go-loop.sh line ~'walk sweep due', 27.4h since the last). It ran 306 minutes, reached 989 of 1011, and was stopped at 09:21 by queue/bin/person-at-mac.sh because the user came back. queue/bin/sweep.sh:585-718 marks it INTERRUPTED (exit 4) and puts the request back on the pile, so the next whole set starts again from walk 1 (another ~5 hours the next time the user steps away). Scripts/playtest-all.sh already takes --only (used by the rotating check at sweep.sh:226), so a remainder run is likely a list of names passed through --only. Traps: only merge when HEAD has no code change since the interrupted run (same rule as 'landed code' in CLAUDE.md: Sources, Scripts, Resources, Vendor, package files); the 3 walks that failed in the last moments are UNCONFIRMED (the stop takes the probe down), so rerun them rather than counting them; version-row-name-walk never finished. Never let a merged result read complete if any walk in the set has no answer. Keep the once-a-day ceiling and the person-away rule. Infrastructure task, no app code.
acceptance: An interrupted full run records which walks it reached, at which commit, and which passed

The next full run, when no app code has landed since, runs only the unreached walks plus the ones that failed, and the merged result counts as one complete full run that can close the standing walk task
When app code has landed since, it says so and runs the whole set as today (or, if cheaper and sound, the unreached walks plus every walk touched by the change; write down which and why)
The time the loop spends on full runs over 48 hours (queue/bin/loop-day.mjs --hours 48) is measured before and after and put in the audit
A drill proves it: a run stopped part way, then the next run touching only the remainder, then the standing task reading the merged result
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: adversarial review before building: (1) an interrupted run reset the once-a-day floor from its own start, so today a stop actually pushed the next whole-set run out a full day AND restarted it from walk one; (2) the 3 failures at the end are casualties of the stop until rerun; (3) a merged record must never read complete with any walk unanswered (a walk that waited for the person prints no line at all); (4) the loop logs seconds per sweep_pass and loop-day draws [t-seconds,t], sweep-size divides seconds by walks: logging the merged sum would paint the gap as walking and make a walk read sub-second; (5) a SIGKILLed remainder recovered by sweep-recover must merge too, so the resume rides in .claimed.json, not in sweep.sh's memory.

Chose: when code has landed since the stop, run the whole set as today (not remainder + touched walks), because any change under Sources can reach any walk and nothing can tell which it did. Chose: the remainder runs as soon as the Mac has been free 15 minutes, inside the floor, because it is the rest of the day's run (the merged record keeps the stopped run's start, so the floor is unchanged). Chose: a run stopped on its own clock is NOT resumed, since that usually means a wedged probe.

built: queue/bin/sweep-resume.mjs (remainderOf, resumable, mergeRuns); sweep-schedule decide() takes the set and returns run:full resume:true; sweep-schedule --resume-plan; sweep.sh run hands playtest-all --only the remainder and writes resumeOf+set into .claimed.json; sweep-record merges from the claim; RECORDED is now checked by the record's log path; summary logs the part's own walks/seconds; sweep.sh what feeds the loop's announcement line; PHOTONZ_SWEEP_RUNNER stand-in for drills. left rough (under the follow-up bar): loop-day.mjs counts a resumed part as one more 'full-set run' (minutes are right, count reads high; only a reader of loop-day sees it). Dashboard's nextFullInHours counts from the stopped run's began, so while a remainder waits for the person it does not say one is waiting (queue-lib sweepState; small, and the remainder runs within minutes of them stepping away).

A whole-set walk run that is stopped now picks up where it stopped: on the same code the next run is only its unanswered walks plus its failures, merged into one complete run of the set (queue/bin/sweep-resume.mjs; sweep-schedule, sweep.sh run, sweep-record).
